title: An unknown member at the top level or in `params` is ignored
notes: PROTOCOL.md §4.1 makes forward compatibility a rule: a receiver MUST ignore a member it does not know, at any depth, in either direction, so that a later wire version can add one without breaking this one. A wire vector can drive only the client-to-server direction, and no client request carries a known nested object whose member could be unknown: `session.hello`'s params hold scalars, an array and a string, and `doc.open`'s params hold one string, so the deepest place this transcript can put an unknown member is a direct member of `params`, beside an unknown top-level member. Both are answered as if they were not there — no `session.error` and no error response — and the unknown subtrees hanging off those unknown members are ignored with them. The hello also claims a capability name the server cannot know, which §10 says is ignored the same way. The server-to-client direction is a receiver obligation a transcript cannot pin, since the reference server never emits a member outside `selvage/1`.
